summary.text: A 35-year-old man with Kartagener syndrome, asthma and atopic dermatitis developed centro facial erythema after a 2013 nasal surgery and presented with reoccurring facial erythematous, oedematous patches and lichenified hyperpigmentation with severe itch and burning pain. External histopathology supported chronic photodermatosis, patch test was unremarkable, ANA screening was negative and topical mometasone, tacrolimus and pimecrolimus did not help.

Oral upadacitinib 15 mg twice daily was started. After 2 weeks pain, itch, sun sensitivity and erythema were improved and swelling was absent, burning and itch scores fell from 7/10 and 9/10 to 0/10 by Week 10, and there were no signs or symptoms of CPD at 2.5 and 6 months follow-up. The patient gained 4 kg within 2 months of treatment, which the authors say could be a side effect.

ambiguities.issue: The 4 kg weight gain is stated as possibly a medication side effect, while the same clause says there was no history of any medical illness, although Kartagener syndrome, asthma and atopic dermatitis are documented earlier in the same case.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat the weight gain as a confirmed adverse drug reaction, and do not record an absent medical history or remove the documented conditions.

evidence.quote: the rapid and sustainable efficacy of upadacitinib as monotherapy in all three patients

ambiguities.issue: The Discussion calls the efficacy monotherapy in all three patients; this applies to patient 1 as written but the later patient 2 text adds topical tacrolimus.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: No separate monotherapy fact is recorded for any patient.

summary.text: A 56-year-old man presented with sun-induced erythematous and hyperpigmented lesions of the face and dorsum of both hands of 1 year duration, severe burning pain and itch. A lesional skin biopsy supported chronic photodermatosis and ANA screening and patch test were negative or unremarkable; histology showed hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, irregular acanthosis and perivascular inflammation.

Topical glucocorticosteroids and antihistamines gave no benefit, ciclosporin gave minimal improvement, neurological symptoms developed while it was tapered and it was then stopped, and hydroxychloroquine was discontinued for an abdominal lesion indicative of a drug reaction. Upadacitinib 15 mg twice daily with topical tacrolimus led to marked improvement within 2 weeks and no side effects for 8 months.

summary.text: A 33-year-old man with atopy presented with scaling erythematous, oedematous patches in sun-exposed areas of the cheeks, nose and forehead starting 6 years previously, severe burning pain and itch, and diffusely demarcated hyperpigmented facial patches with lichenification and scales. Autoimmune screening including ANA and an external patch test were negative and external histopathology supported chronic photodermatosis.

Topical and systemic glucocorticosteroids and topical pimecrolimus and tacrolimus worsened the condition, systemic glucocorticosteroids were associated with hypertension and rebound after tapering, and dupilumab was discontinued after lesions worsened. A photosensitivity test caused erythema and itchiness within 24 h. Upadacitinib 15 mg twice daily brought marked improvement within 2 weeks and improved quality of life, with burning pain and itch scores of 10/10 falling to 0/10 by Week 10.

Table 1 prints bare scores such as 7/10; the scale name NRS-11 is stated in the case text, and text ranges (9–10/10) differ from single table values (9/10 or 10/10) without being a conflict.
